learningObjective: Describe the role of a kernel registry (a mapping from op signature to concrete implementation) in a runtime that supports multiple backends and dtypes.

canonicalClaims.claim: A kernel registry is a runtime lookup table that maps op signature keys (op name, device, dtype, layout, …) to concrete implementations; the dispatcher queries it to route a call to the correct backend kernel.
conditions: The runtime supports multiple backends and needs to route ops dynamically.
Registrations are populated at library load or plugin discovery.
nonImplications: Does not imply the registry stores kernel binaries; it stores callable references.
Does not imply that missing registrations trigger JIT compilation; that is a separate mechanism.

misconceptions.claim: The kernel registry is a JIT compilation cache.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A JIT cache stores compiled artifacts keyed by inputs/shapes; a registry maps op signatures to implementations that already exist.

misconceptions.claim: The registry is the cost model.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A cost model predicts kernel latency; the registry routes to the implementation.
Hardware descriptors (SM count, warp size) belong to a device query API, not to the op-implementation table.

misconceptions.claim: Kernel registration always happens at compile time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Many runtimes register at library load via static initializers or dynamic plugin discovery.
